citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The facility’s grooming room is in need of cleaning and general housekeeping. There was a heavy accumulation of dust
on storage shelves, boxes, miscellaneous items and tables in the room, including a table with medications and other
medical supplies. Several cobwebs were observed along the walls, in corners, and near shelves and tables including one
approximately 2ft X 2ft in size. In a corner of the room near a door, there was an open bag of shredded paper bedding
with loose pieces accumulated in a pile covering approximately 3ft X 4ft of floor space. Failure to adequately clean animal
use areas or any supply storage areas may attract unwanted rodents or other pests and contribute to the spread of
disease or illness. Premises where housing facilities are located, including surrounding buildings and surrounding
grounds, and other animal areas must be kept and in good repair to protect the animals from injury, to prevent the
harborage of pests, and to facilitate the husbandry practices required in this subpart. A system of maintaining effective
housekeeping practices must be in place to protect the health and well-being of the animals.
Correct by 10/29/2026.

The licensee has not been following the attending veterinarian’s approved schedule for the sampling of parasites and
other pests for dogs. According to the facility’s Program of Veterinary Care (PVC) for Dogs, 1-3 adult dogs will be tested
each year for heartworm disease, and 1-3 adult dogs will have a fecal float annually. The last documented heartworm test
results and fecal test results were over 2 years ago, 07/29/2024. Failure to conduct sampling and treatment for parasites
and other pests in accordance with the attending veterinarian’s approved schedule can expose the animals to increased
disease risk and can delay treatment. The licensee must ensure that sampling and treatment of parasites and other pests
(including fleas, worms, coccidia, giardia, and heartworm) are followed in accordance with the schedule approved by the
attending veterinarian.
Correct by 10/29/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
